description: Semi-arid poplar box (Eucalyptus populnea) woodland with shrub thickets
locality: Pastoral property 'Oakvale', 115 km south of Bourke, New South Wales
vegetation: Poplar box woodland: Eucalyptus populnea (26/ha) on slopes and depressions, E. intertexta (10/ha) on ridges; tree canopies cover 13% of the ground. Beneath each tree a shrub thicket dominated by Eremophila mitchellii and Geijera parviflora; interthicket areas dominated by Acacia aneura, Senna artemisiodes ssp. filifolia, S. artemisiodes ssp. artemisiodes and Eremophila bowmanii var. bowmanii; Eremophila sturtii and Dodonaea viscosa ssp. spatulata in both. Shrub density about 4800/ha. Herbaceous layer of annual forbs and grasses (0-150 g/m2/year).
soil type: Massive red earth (typic durargid), no A2 horizon, indurated layer of stone or bedrock at 60-80 cm
geomorphology: Near the centre of a large pediplain; very gently undulating, rises 0.5-1 km apart, slopes 1-1.5%
fire history: Fire chance reduced from one in 5 years to one in 15-20 years by fewer fires and grazing-driven shift to shrub dominance (Walker 1981). Experimental plots burnt once, October 1977 onwards; winter low-fuel fires 15 July 1978 and 18 July 1979.
grazing: 108-ha exclosure fenced in 1977 to exclude sheep, cattle, goats and pigs but not kangaroos
notes: Coordinates 146°30'E, 30°55'S as printed (Methods p.65), converted to decimal degrees. Potential evaporation is US class A pan; rainfall evenly distributed, monthly CV 70% (July) to 180% (February). Four areas (two of E. intertexta, two of E. populnea), each with 24 plots of 15 x 21 m spanning a tree thicket and an interthicket area.
